headlines.hero: 8 models tested once on unseen seasons. 5 passed, 3 failed.
headlines.scoreboard: 5 passed, 3 failed, 2 negative results, 1 not yet tested.
headlines.chart: The NFLELO model beat Elo in all 6 seasons. The market is 0.010 Brier ahead.

models.name: NFLELO model
models.what: Win chance per game from Elo, efficiency and the starting quarterback.
models.reading: Beat Elo in all six seasons. The market is still ahead.

primary.label: Brier score, NFLELO model minus Elo (lower is better)

also.text: Brier 0.2195 against Elo 0.2231 and the Vegas market 0.2096

models.name: Margin model
models.what: The full spread of possible final margins.
models.reading: Edge over Elo not proven: the interval includes zero.

primary.label: Average margin error in points, model minus Elo's spread (lower is better)

also.text: Error 10.126 points against Elo 10.185 and the market line 9.764

models.name: Playoff odds
models.reading: Strength shocks improved the forecast, and the odds were calibrated.

primary.label: Made-playoffs Brier score, with strength shocks minus without (lower is better)

also.text: The tiebreaker code reproduces all 48 actual conference seedings, 2002 to 2025

models.name: Lineup values
models.what: A value per player from box scores, plus probable lineups.
models.reading: Lineups added nothing measurable, so no holdout was spent.

primary.label: Brier score, best lineup model minus the NFLELO model (lower is better)

also.text: Smaller steps: +0.000 and +0.000; every interval includes zero

models.name: On-field player ratings
models.what: A plus-minus rating for every player, from 177,545 plays.
models.reading: Beat team ratings, lost to summed box-score values.

primary.label: Play-level squared error, RAPM minus box-score values (lower is better)

models.name: Shadow model
models.what: A team-strength rating (Kalman filter) that carries its own uncertainty.
models.reading: Narrowly missed on development seasons. Running as a live shadow.

primary.label: Brier score, shadow model minus NFLELO model (lower is better)

models.name: Play outcome model
models.what: The full distribution of yards a play can gain.
models.reading: Beat the baseline every season. Players add little.

primary.label: Yards error (CRPS), call view: model minus baseline (lower is better)

models.name: Win-probability model
models.what: Win chance at every snap, with no market input.
models.reading: Beats nflfastR. The Vegas-based probability is still better.

primary.label: Brier score, our model minus nflfastR (lower is better)

also.text: Against the Vegas-based probability: +0.006 [+0.004, +0.009] (Vegas is better)

models.name: Fourth-down tool
models.what: Go, kick or punt, compared in win probability.
models.reading: Field goal and punt parts passed; conversion estimates were off.

primary.label: Go-for-it conversion calibration error (ECE) against its limit (lower is better)

also.text: Field goal make rate calibration 0.011: passed
Punts: -0.105 [-0.126, -0.086] yards of error against the by-spot baseline: passed

models.name: Early-down play calling
models.what: Run or pass, and personnel, on early downs.
models.reading: Recommended mix beats actual play calling. Defenses would adapt.

primary.label: EPA per early-down play, recommended mix minus observed (higher is better)

also.text: Placebo check, should be about zero: +0.006 [-0.001, +0.012]

models.name: NFLELO model upgrades
models.what: Five upgrades to the NFLELO model.
models.reading: No upgrade beat the shadow model beyond noise.

primary.label: Brier score, best upgrade minus the shadow model (lower is better)

findings.title: The quarterback is most of the story.
findings.text: Nearly all of the gain over Elo comes from knowing the starting QB.

findings.title: Player credit beats team ratings.
findings.text: On-field plus-minus adds nothing beyond box-score credit.

findings.title: Elo's edge is memory.
findings.text: Elo wins weeks 1 to 4; our features win weeks 10 to 18.

findings.title: The market is still better at game prediction.
